scenario: A 72-year-old woman has atrial fibrillation on the tracing, a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 4, and no valve replacement. She is rate-controlled and feels fine. A classmate starts aspirin because she has no symptoms.
question: What stroke prevention fits the score, and why is feeling fine not protective?
options: No drug, because rate control also prevents stroke
Dual antiplatelet therapy as the equal of an anticoagulant
Cardioversion today without anticoagulation, because the duration is unknown
Anticoagulation. Aspirin is not enough at this score
correctAnswer: Anticoagulation. Aspirin is not enough at this score
citation: Joglar JA, et al. 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation. Circulation. 2024.
examTakeaway: Nonvalvular atrial fibrillation with an elevated CHA2DS2-VASc score gets anticoagulation. Aspirin is not the substitute.
